description: Analogy means finding a similarity or a relationship. It involves understanding the underlying logic between given words, letters, or numbers to discover a new relationship based on that same pattern.

sections.title: Word Analogy
sections.description: Identifying a meaningful relationship between two words, which is often based on general knowledge and vocabulary.

key_concepts.explanation: Relationships based on words having similar meanings or entirely opposite meanings.
A scenario where one event is the direct result or consequence of another event.

cases.condition: When the relationship is between Product and Raw Material

sections.title: Letter Analogy
sections.description: Questions based on the position of letters in the English alphabet and identifying the patterns connecting them.

key_concepts.explanation: The specific numerical value of each letter in the alphabet when counted from left to right.
Pairs of letters whose numerical positions in the alphabet always sum up to exactly 27.

cases.condition: Fixed Addition or Subtraction in Letters
results: The logic can follow a sequential pattern like +1, +2, +3.
Transformations can also be based on differentiating between Vowels and Consonants.

sections.title: Number Analogy
sections.description: Discovering the mathematical logic, patterns, or operations hidden between a given set of numbers.

key_concepts.explanation: A whole number greater than 1 that cannot be exactly divided by any whole number other than itself and 1 (e.g., 2, 3, 5, 7).

sections.title: Solving Strategy
sections.description: A systematic and structured approach to solve analogy questions with maximum speed and accuracy.

steps.title: Identify the Logic
steps.detail: Carefully observe and find the exact logical relationship between the first two elements provided in the question.

steps.title: Analyze the Options
steps.detail: Apply the identified logic consistently to all the given multiple-choice options.

steps.title: Use Elimination Method
steps.detail: Quickly eliminate the options that clearly do not match the basic logic to narrow down to the correct answer.
